support.p:
Size assuming the identification as No. 10294 is correct.
Script: 'bru tsha.
Lines per folio: 9; 3 on fol. 6b.
Orthography:
- bindu for m
- da drags (6b3: pha rol du phyind pa'i)
- palatalization of ma
- abbreviations (for thams cad, bcu gcig, yon tan, etc.)
- Na for med
- sanskritized words ('bu' ta for sangs rgyas)
- numerals used for numbers
- additional prefix b- (e.g., bsgom pa)
- superabundant 'a rjes 'jug (e.g., 'di')
- vertical ligature for d+ng (looking like rng)
- expected ba/bo often written like pa/po
Numerous interlinear annotations (some of which corrections) and marginal annotations.

adminInfo.note: The signature above the first line on fol. 1a seems to read "phyi la 588", as reported in [S635TW6P]: 53, but there is no corresponding entry with this signature in the [8H6M69W4]. This instance could correspond to the entry No. 10294 reported with the signature "phyi ma 586", with matching title, author, and number of folios (sher snying gi rgya cher 'grel bzhugs so; shAkya'i dge slong byang chub ye shes kyis; 'bru tsha; 6 f.; 64.5x10.5cm).

person.persName: slob dpon chen po dpal mar me mdzad ye shes
paN+Di ta dI paM ka ra
ma hA paN+Di ta mar me mdzad ye shes
dpal mar me mdzad dpal ye shes zhabs
dge slong blo ldan shes rab
rngog dge slong blo ldan shes rab
person.note:
See [BAQ9MH4T]: 193 for the main events of his life.
Three manuscript editions of his writings and translations were deposited respectively in rNgog Blo ldan shes rab's tomb, in the monastery of gSang phu (probably in the main assembly hall), and in Drin las kyi sde (ID:4357) ([7FZ3B926]: 107).

Further holy places associated to him are: Ze thang, Grwa thang and rMog po ([647FFPZR]: 545, based on [Q3KCZX7B]: 38). Remembered for thirteen distinguished objects (such as royal insignia and religious articles), which could be objects of his clan ([4LDAV8UH]: 95.).

His dates can be approximated as 1070-1130.
He is possibly the same person as Byang 'chad khyung (ID:6382), as [NA9AMDH6] states that Khyung rin chen grags held Byang 'chad (ID:4416) and taught Sa chen (ID:4205) there ([647FFPZR]: 543). [CJ75QQKN]: 339 (fol. 8a/170a1-3). dMar ston's Zhib mo rdo rje ([RA3FK3BK]: 134 and 137), on the other hand, distinguish the two figures and places Sa chen's studies with Khyung at Nyang stod byang 'chad, and those with Khyung rin chen grags at Nyang stod.
On the reference to Khyung as "slang pa/slang pha/slang pha ba" (understood as a regionalism for "glang pa/glang pha ba," see [WL39GVT5]: 940.

shag kya'i dge slong byang ye

person.note: Dates according to [2V6H2FBU]: 24, n. 70 ("Since Ar was invited as a dge bshes to a monastery in 1076, it is hard to believe that he was not at least 20 years old, which would put his birth-date at least in 1056. The last trace of his existence is in 1144 when he took over the head of rgyal lha khang.").

[MGPRHX73]: 58, n. 24 cites an 18th century work that argues that "gzhon nu tshul khrims" is the real name of 'Dul 'dzin dkar mo (ID:3820) and "shes rab 'bum" that of his student dKar chung ring mo (ID:3821).

person.persName: dge bshes ston pa chen po
person.note:
Celibate householder from the Byang region, chief disciple of Atiśa (ID: 3745) ([Q922IUFM]: 30).
dGe 'dun grub pa (ID:7060) is renowned as his reincarnation and his 'Brom ston-like qualities are described ([BKUHJCNA]: 787-790).

person.note: Floruit 1095–1135. [YF8Z2ZGH]: 332 "rGya dmar pa was not only fully learned, but also possessed numerous Tantric secret precepts."

gtsang nags phug pa brtson 'grus seng ge

person.note: Van der Kuijp ([H9MPLMTV]) proposed the dates (?-1185). The terminus ante quem for gTsang nag pa's death was pushed to 1192 by Schwabland ([Q8WU9EDW]: 794, n. 3) on account of the date of Khro pu lo tsA ba (ID:3878)'s studies with gTsang nag pa. This date was corrected to 1195 based on Khro phu lo tsA ba's biography (van der Kuijp, personal communication).

person.persName: rma bya rtsod pa'i seng ge
person.note: rMa bya's name is rendered in Tangut as Po tjɨj ˑjɨr, in which po tjɨj is a phonetic transcription of "bodhi" [=Tib. byang chub], whereas ˑjɨr means "diligence" [=Tib. brtson 'grus].

person.persName: phag mo gru pa rdo rje rgyal po
dpal chos kyi rje 'gro ba'i mgon po
person.note: The nickname "chos tsha ba" is explained in [WBWSEPQX]: 4b (lar mtshan nyid kyi grwa sar lo mang du bzhugs te | khams pa yar 'dug pa la chos tsha ba'i grags pa thob). Sho sgom (ID:3857), Dus gsum mkhyen pa (ID:3855) and Phag mo gru pa (ID:3856) are known as the "grub thob mi gsum" and as the "khams pa mi gsum."

Same person as gTsang nags phug pa 'jam dbyangs shes rab 'od zer (ID:6640)? Late 13th-early 14th c. according to van der Kuijp ([H9MPLMTV]: 22). Late 12th-early 13th c. according to [MX3PRVV2]: 3/16 and n. 4. Considered to be identical with gNyal zhig's student 'Jam dbyangs gsar ma ([4LWBNM7B]: 121). Important master in the Dro lineage of the Kālacakra ([MX3PRVV2]). A list of his compositions is discussed in [MX3PRVV2]: 7-8/16.

person.persName: gnyal zhig po 'jam pa'i rdo rje
gnyal pa zhig po 'jam pa'i rdo rje
dmyal zhig po 'jam pa'i rdo rje
yul dbus kyi slob dpon 'jam pa'i rdo rje
person.note: Fl. late 12th to early 13th c. [MPRU5QUC] records the name of this abbot as "'Jam dpal seng ge." He received the name "'jam pa'i rdo rje" during a tantric initiation ([5632TFMN]: 312 and n. 11). [AT6DUUJJ]: 23 discusses his dates, suggesting he lived towards the end of the 12th century.. [5632TFMN]: 313 suggests he may have passed away in ca. 1227.

person.persName: chos grags gnyis pa gzhon nu rin chen
chos grwa gsar ma gzhon nu rin chen
person.note: Fl. late 13th to early 14th c. We assume that the gZhon nu rin chen who was abbot of gSang phu is the same person as the author of the two works by gZhon nu rin chen. The latter is characterized in [8H6M69W4], No. 15506, as the "student of Nyang" (nyang gi slob ma), which, in view of the colophon of (ID:4625), is Nyang bran pa Chos kyi ye shes (ID:3876) rather than Nyang bran pa Chos kyi seng ge (ID:3844).

bibl.author: ar byang chub ye shes
bibl.note:
Commentary based on another commentary by someone referred to as "Jo bo" (= Atiśa (ID:3745), or Jo bo 'bum (ID:5611)?) composed in "bsam yangs" (maybe for bSam yas?).
The author refers to the interpretation by 'Brom ston (ID:6284) and other Tibetan scholars (referred to as “dags po” and “khyung po”).
The text contains a number of Sanskrit expressions transcribed in Tibetan (e.g., ’bu dha, bo de sa dha, lo ga).
This work may correspond to the "phar phyin" listed in the Tho yig ([5RXEUKD9]: 529, No. 11502: ar byang chub ye shes kyi phar phyin), see (ID:6536).

bibl.title: shes rab kyi pha rol du phyin pa'i man ngag gi bstan bcos mngon par rtogs pa'i rgyan ces bya ba'i 'grel pa rnaM par 'byed pa
ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་དུ་ཕྱིན་པའི་མན་ངག་གི་བསྟན་བཅོས་མངོན་པར་རྟོགས་པའི་རྒྱན་ཅེས་བྱ་བའི་འགྲེལ་པ་རྣཾ་པར་འབྱེད་པ
mngon rtogs rgyan gyi 'grel ba rnam 'byed ces bya ba'i 'grel pa rnam par 'byed pa
mngon rtogs rgyan gyi 'grel pa rnam 'byed
mngon rtogs rgyan gyi 'grel ba rnam 'byed ces bya ba
bibl.author: ar byang chub ye shes
bibl.note:
The title of the text in the colophon and section colophons indicate that it is a commentary on the Abhisamayālaṅkāravṛtti (ID:3711). The discussion on the title of the base text (see (ID:4454), fol. 35b6) refers to the Tibetan expressions corresponding to the Sanskrit "prajñāpāramita," "upadeśa," "śāstra," "abhisamaya," "ālaṃkāra." It does not explain the word "vṛtti," but goes stating "'grel pa 'di la don gsum ste...". The end of the text systematically comments on the words of Haribhadra's Vṛtti, and large portions are commented before that (such as the dgos 'brel section). It remains to be established if the whole Vṛtti is commented upon in the body of the text. Also referred to is Haribhadra’s Abhisamayālaṅkārālokā (ID:3709) – referred to as the “large commentary” ('grel chen) - although the author frequently disagrees with Haribhadra's interpretation - and the commentaries of Bhadantavimuktisena (ID:5548) and Āryavimuktisena (ID:3708), and the views of “’bum pa” (Sthirapala (ID:5611). Also mentioned in the text are notably the views of Dharmottara (ID:3780), Atiśa (ID:3745), 'Brom ston (ID:3827), an unidentified "dge bshes," as well as those of lesser known figures.
In the incipit, the author refers to the teaching of Blo ldan shes rab (ID:3786) - to whom the numerous references to "maha/mahA" seem to refer - Rin chen grags (ID:3809), and Shes rab 'bar (ID:3807). The latter is also mentioned in the closing verses.
The introductory verse echoes that in the Shes rab pha rol phyin pa sdud pa tshigs su bcad pa'i rnam par bshad pa (ID:4457) by the same author.
The introductory section gives the lineage of Prajñāpāramitā. The author lists Indic commentators’ names up to Ratnākaraśānti (ID:5550), Prajñākaramati (ID:6137), Ku lan ta, and Ratnakīrti, but does not refer to Abhayākaragupta's Marmakaumudī.

bibl.author: ar byang chub ye shes
bibl.note:
This commentary on the Sañcayagāthā (ID:3693) may correspond to the work listed by A khu ching shes rab rgya mtsho in his Tho yig ([5RXEUKD9]: 529, No. 11503: [ar byang chub ye shes kyi] mdo sdud pa). The explanation of the words of the base text is preceded by an introduction that includes an outline of Prajñāpāramitā literature. The author refers to other commentaries on the text (one referred to as “new commentary”), and to the interpretation of “lo tsa ba” (rNgog Blo ldan shes rab) and “’bum” (i.e., ’Bum phrag gsum pa, brTan skyong/Sthirapāla), and claims to have followed mainly the commentary of Buddhaśrījñāna.
The introductory verse echoes that of the Shes rab kyi pha rol du phyin pa'i man ngag gi bstan bcos mngon par rtogs pa'i rgyan ces bya ba'i 'grel pa rnaM par 'byed pa (ID:4455) by the same author.
Two instances of the work are extant - (ID:4456) and (ID:5892) - with different, but partially overlapping, annotations.
